description:
The Call of the Open Road

The Giramondo is a celebration of Masi’s enduring spirit of adventure. Rooted in the legacy of Faliero Masi and his relentless passion for exploration, this bike is built for those who dream of long rides and endless horizons. Inspired by Masi’s gravel origins, the Giramondo embraces the philosophy of discovery, encouraging riders to venture beyond the beaten path and explore the world on two wheels.

Crafted from high-quality chromoly steel, the Giramondo carries the heart of Masi’s traditional craftsmanship. Steel’s unparalleled durability and resilience make it the perfect material for touring bikes. Its ability to withstand the rigors of unpredictable roads ensures that no journey is too far or too demanding. Beyond its strength, steel’s repairability provides a layer of reassurance. Even in the most remote regions, a skilled mechanic can easily weld and restore a steel frame — a testament to the Giramondo’s practicality and reliability.

The Giramondo is equipped with wide tires for superior traction and control, adapting effortlessly to gravel paths, dirt trails, and rugged landscapes. Its frame is designed to accommodate all forms of bikepacking gear, including racks, fenders, and multiple bottle mounts. Whether embarking on a weekend escape or a months-long expedition, this bike is your steadfast companion, ready to carry you and your essentials across continents.

Every detail of the Giramondo echoes the adventurous spirit of its namesake. Just as Faliero Masi once pursued the thrill of the unknown, modern-day riders can follow in his footsteps — embracing the joy of exploration and the freedom of the open road. With every pedal stroke, Giramondo encourages you to write your own story of discovery.

Giramondo invites you to embrace the spirit of adventure. Through winding mountain passes, endless gravel roads, and remote countryside trails, this Masi classic is built to withstand the miles and make every journey unforgettable. True to the legacy of Masi, it’s not just a bike — it’s a passport to the world.
